The first cut wrote a comment claiming both spellings worked everywhere and then implemented neither half: validate still parsed only --read-only, so --dry-run ran the full write path on the very command the issue names, and parseArgs silently dropped --read-only on archive, migrate, sync and generate, where archive moved and deleted source files. Both reviews caught it by execution. Now both spellings route through one isReadOnly helper across validate, compile, complete, archive, migrate and sync. The default stays a writer, decided rather than left implicit: closeout depends on the reconciliation, and flipping it trades a surprising write for a silent omission people forget to run. Shipping without an automated test for the flag parse is what let the false claim survive; the CLI-level check that caught it afterwards is not a substitute. |

**Known hazards for future sprints:**
- The document-level fallback in roadmap-source-store.ts must run the same reparse-and-compare over-reach check as the surgical path. Without it an anchored or aliased status silently mutates a second sprint.
- yaml Document toString wraps at 80 columns by default. Pass lineWidth 0 anywhere the previous code used stringify with lineWidth 0, or every long authored note reflows.
- src/core/roadmap-source-patch.ts is the comment-preserving path and must not be extended to shapes it declines.
- parseArgs in roadmap.ts silently drops unknown flags, so a new flag name is accepted and ignored rather than rejected. Adding an alias means routing every writing subcommand through one helper.
- Checking that a test is discriminating requires reverting the specific call site. Stashing the file is a no-op when the code under test is already committed.
